package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external server during installation. The code is obfuscated and embedded in the setup.py file, which is executed automatically when the package is installed, enabling credential theft without user knowledge.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive credential files and transmits their contents to an external server during package installation, which is not expected behavior for a legitimate package.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal setup.py should only handle package installation logic and not access or transmit user credentials. This code violates user trust by exfiltrating private keys and credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may read configuration files for setup, but they should never transmit sensitive data to external servers, especially during installation.
key_indicators: Use of requests.post to external domain during install
Execution of exfiltration logic at install-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code decodes and executes a base64-encoded payload that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and sends it to https://malicious.example.com/upload, enabling stealthy credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of base64-encoded payloads in setup.py is a common obfuscation technique to hide malicious actions, such as credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts do not obfuscate code or execute hidden payloads, especially those that access sensitive files and perform network exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64 encoding may be used for data handling, but not for hiding executable code in installation scripts.
key_indicators: Presence of base64-encoded executable payload in setup.py
Dynamic execution of decoded code via exec()
Encoded payload accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa and performs network exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User installs the 'pymafka' package from PyPI, triggering setup.py execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py reads sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential data is collected from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: Collected credentials are exfiltrated to https://malicious.example.com/upload via HTTPS POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's private keys and credentials.

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials during package installation
Execution of base64-decoded payloads in setup.py
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded external domains during install
file_indicators: setup.py containing base64-encoded strings and exec() calls
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation scripts (setup.py) for access to sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials, especially when combined with outbound network requests to external domains. Flag any use of base64-encoded payloads that are decoded and executed at install-time. Block or alert on HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious.example.com/upload originating from installation scripts.
